TL;DR

Effectively identifying top candidates and evaluating technical skills are crucial difficulties for firms operating in the fast-paced software development industry. IT assessment tools, which provide organized platforms to examine coding proficiency, problem-solving skills, and algorithmic thinking, have become essential in this process. These tools are essential for building effective tech teams and encouraging innovation, whether they are utilized for recruiting, skill development, or interview practice.

This article explores the best IT assessment tools that are being used by organizations to hire tech talent. Every tool has different features and capabilities; these range from coding challenge platforms to real-time feedback and thorough skill evaluations. Businesses can streamline their developer evaluation processes and make sure they are utilizing the best tools available in today's competitive landscape by having a clear understanding of their features and benefits.

## Best IT Assessment Tools

The best IT assessment tools not only evaluate tech talents but also should be cost-effective. This cost reduction ultimately leads to an increase in the efficiency of the organization.

We will explore the top 10 IT assessment tools that can help you hire the best IT talents for your business.

### 1. WeCP

WeCP is the leading platform in the industry for AI-powered IT assessments. Employers can hire IT talent from anywhere in the world by using its technical screening and remote interviewing services. You can design tests with WeCP that mimic actual workplaces to get a better picture of how candidates will perform there.

WeCP offers recruiters a better grasp of a candidate's aptitudes with its database of over 200k questions. It assesses not just the final performance but also the approach, logic, design, and even soft skills.

WeCP is a helpful tool if you want to assess people for long-term success in addition to their short-term talents.

Features

  • Access over 200k+ technical questions across various domains.
  • WeCP AI Copilot for creating skill-focused assessments.
  • Collaborative code editor to conduct technical assessments.
  • Real-time code quality feedback.
  • Proctored assessments that track candidate’s misconduct and alerts in real-time.
  • Provides insights with a comprehensive analytics report.

Pricing

WeCP offers a 7-day free trial with limited features.

  • Price: $240 per month
  • Plans available: Premium, Custom and Enterprise

Organizations can select plans according to their needs, whether they need to enhance staff skills or test potential candidate skills.

In the current recruiting market, AI’s use case in this industry could be easily seen. WeCP is enhancing the hiring experiences of its clients by utilizing this technical marvel. With merely a text request, WeCP's AI can produce highly relevant, intuitive, and customizable tech assessments. It is not a surprise that they received a 4.8 out of 5 G2 review rating.

### 2. HackerRank

HackerRank helps to hire technical talent and provides a range of tools and services to help businesses evaluate candidates effectively. It gives companies the ability to create code challenges and competitions that are tailored to their specific needs.

HackerRank offers a vast library of pre-made coding assessments in a variety of topics and degrees of difficulty. These difficulties allow businesses to swiftly build up evaluations rather than having to start from zero.

Features

  • IT assessment to evaluate a candidate's aptitude and ability in coding.
  • AI-powered plagiarism detection for code review and integrity preservation.
  • Collaborative tool for conducting IT interviews.
  • Role-based assessment according to that role's seniority.

Pricing

  • Pricing: $100 per month, $450 per month
  • Plans available: Starter, Pro and Custom

One of the few hiring platforms using AI to improve hiring efficiency is HackerRank. They are reducing time to hire by utilizing AI to compose interview questions and provide automated transcriptions of interviews, and increasing hiring efficiency by using AI-derived signals to analyze code quality and effort analysis to give hiring managers important insights.

### 3. HackerEarth

Companies can design customized coding challenges and competitions using HackerEarth to meet their unique needs. Employers can evaluate candidates' ways of managing different programming problems, problem-solving capabilities, and coding abilities with the help of these challenges.

Additionally, HackerEarth offers tests to evaluate candidates' soft skills, such as aptitude, reasoning, and communication. This consists of scenario-based questions that evaluate problem-solving skills as well as written communication.

Features

  • Collaborative tool for conducting real-time virtual interviews and automating interview summaries.
  • Talent assessment to evaluate a candidate's coding and problem-solving skills using an integrated IDE.
  • Logic reasoning and scenario-based tests to gauge a candidate's aptitude for solving problems.

Pricing

  • Pricing: $209/mo, $419/mo
  • Plans available: Starter, Custom and Enterprise

Originally designed as a venue for hackathons and competitive programming, HackerEarth has expanded to include a range of tools and assessments targeted at developers. Apart from endorsing instructional events and initiatives aimed at nurturing technical and coding skills, HackerEarth also engages in efforts that foster inclusivity and diversity within the technology sector.

### 4. Mettl

Mettl offers a variety of adaptable evaluation modules made especially for positions in information technology. Technical aptitude, coding expertise, problem-solving skills, and domain-specific knowledge pertinent to IT positions can all be evaluated in these tests.

To guarantee the security and integrity of the assessment process, Mettl offers comprehensive proctoring features that facilitate remote assessments. This involves tracking videos, tracking browser activity, and implementing additional security protocols to stop cheating.

### Features

  • Real-time coding environment that accepts a variety of programming languages, including C++, Java, and others, and stores the candidate's code session for the interviewer to evaluate.
  • Real-time remote proctoring and reports for hiring managers.
  • Provides assessments to evaluate behavioral competencies and soft skills, like teamwork, communication, and flexibility, that are essential for IT professionals.

Pricing

Contact the Mettl support team.

The comprehensive analytics and reports generated by Mettl's evaluations offer valuable insights into the performance and skill levels of candidates. Making data-driven decisions throughout the hiring process or staff development initiatives is made easier with the help of these insights.

### 5. iMocha

To make it easier for recruiters to find and select technical talent, iMocha provides IT assessment tools. You can assess a variety of IT domains, including coding, data science, machine learning, cybersecurity, and more, with the use of an AI-powered.

iMocha has a reporting feature that offers insights into the candidate's strengths and weaknesses. Additionally, it includes live whiteboard interviews, AI-LogicBox, a patented pseudo-coding platform, and recorded and live coding to help virtually evaluate candidates' technical and problem-solving abilities.

Features

  • Provides various pre-employment tests covering coding, aptitude, and domain-specific expertise required for IT assessment.
  • AI-powered proctoring measures that record images, sounds, and videos in real-time.
  • The analytics dashboard feature provides actionable insights to assess the performance of candidates.
  • Additionally, it provides APIs for platform integration and customization.

Pricing

  • Pricing: $5000 per year
  • Plans available: Premium, Custom

In addition to being among the top tools for IT assessments, iMocha offers additional services that support workforce talent development and management. The new iMocha system, the Skill Intelligence Cloud, manages reskilling and upskilling activities when a candidate joins the company.

### 6. Coderpad

Hiring managers can quickly determine high-quality IT talents by conducting interviews in the candidate's preferred language with Coderpad's IT assessment tools.

Coderpad makes remote and on-site evaluation easier. It provides tools to conduct collaborative interviews for remote hiring, which consist of a whiteboarding tool and an online ide for pair programming.

### Features

  • Live collaborative online IDE for paired programming.
  • A platform for take-home assignments.
  • Digital whiteboard tool for remote interview.
  • Integration with the company’s existing recruiting software like ATS and scheduling tools.

Pricing

  • Pricing: $840/year, $3900/year
  • Plans available: Free, Starter, Team and Custom

Apart from facilitating live paired programming interviews between large organizations and applicants globally, Codepad was established as a cost-effective substitute for feature-rich HR software. Additionally, it provided access to top-notch technologies for talent screening and competitiveness to smaller startups—which lack the sophisticated tools and resources of their larger competitors.

### 7. Coderbyte

Coderbyte is an IT assessment tool for engineering and technical job interview processes. These IT assessments include mobile, DevOps, front-end, and data science. Additionally, they offer a whiteboarding tool for remote interviews as well as a collaboration platform with Jupyter Notebooks, a real-time code editor.

Through the use of tutorials, articles, and coding challenges, candidates can effectively hone their technical skills and get ready for exams by utilizing Coderbyte's instructional resources.

Features

  • Coding assessment tool with automatic grading from a collection of more than 1,000 problems, 100 abilities, and 30+ languages.
  • Live IDE featuring a whiteboard, video, and frameworks.
  • Bring home practical assignments.
  • Evaluations of personality tests.

### Pricing

Pricing: $199/mo, $1699/year

Plans available: Premium

Over 1000 firms have switched from leading hiring platforms to Coderbyte, which supports over 3000 brands such as Zoominfo, stability.ai, and Rohde & Schwarz. It also provides integration with recruiting software like Workable, Greenhouse, Lever, and Zapier.

### 8. Codility

Codility gives businesses the ability to design and manage code challenges that evaluate applicant's IT proficiency. Employers can alter tasks on Codility to match particular job specifications and position-specific technical competencies. This customization consists of defining programming languages and frameworks, creating various kinds of coding difficulties, and modifying the degree of difficulty.

Codility provides comprehensive data and reports on the performance of applicants in assessments. Recruiters have access to metrics such as code correctness, efficiency, performance in a range of test cases, and comparative analysis of candidates.

Features

  • Codelive is a collaborative interviewing tool that combines pair programming, video conferencing, an IDE, and whiteboard features.
  • Codecheck is an online skill assessment tool to test job-relevant skills with AI assistants for providing assessment templates and integrity features like proctoring and cheating detection.

Pricing

  • Pricing: $1200/ann, $5000/ann
  • Plans available: Starter, Scale and Enterprise

Codility also offers tools for ATS and other HR product integration. This enables a smooth synchronization of assessment results and candidate profiles with the company's hiring process.

### 9. CodeSignal

Companies can get talent evaluations, real-world projects, coding competitions, tailored instruction, coding challenges, and comprehensive feedback from CodeSignal, a cloud-based AI platform for IT skill assessment.

To help managers in decision-making, CodeSignal offers comprehensive statistics and insights on applicant performance. It also provides access to a sizable and vibrant developer community for interaction and education.

Features

  • A built-in plagiarism checker and a code editor with more than 70 coding languages.
  • Offers a pre-screening and remote interviewing tool equipped with cutting-edge security features.
  • Retraining and upskilling services to meet business demands.

Pricing

Contact the sales team for pricing information.

CodeSignal has unveiled Cosmo, an AI-driven bot that helps users pick up technical skills. It decided to use gamification to commercialize its users. Cosmo initially provides users with certain energy bars to help them with their doubts when they ask queries. These energy bars, however, get shorter as more questions are posed. This energy bar refuels every four hours.

They charge $24.99 per month for an endless supply of energy bars.

### 10. CodeInterview

CodeInterview is a cloud-based online code interview tool that provides online code editors and compilers for all widely used languages to enable interviewers and candidates to collaborate in real-time.

Additionally, CodeInterview provides solutions for talent development. This includes personalized IT training, a gamified practice environment, and personalized learning paths with the help of their in-house AI Guide, Cosmo.

Features

  • Coding and take-home project assignment creation.
  • About 30+ programming languages and frameworks are available.
  • For remote interviews, whiteboard mode for audio and video calls is available.
  • Integrated browser plugin for conducting a productive front-end interview

Hiring managers can save questions in more than 30 programming languages with CodeInterview and use them again for assessments and interviews. It offers integrated video and audio capabilities for a smooth, cooperative interviewing process. Additionally, it includes a note-taking function so that the recruiting team can later compare and evaluate applicants.

## Conclusion

It is critical to use the best IT assessment tools to evaluate technical proficiency, improve talent acquisition decision-making, and promote ongoing skill development. With the help of these tools, businesses can streamline their IT recruitment and develop a highly skilled workforce that can spur innovation and satisfy changing market expectations.

WeCP offers the most comprehensive IT assessment tool, so you can maximize the performance of your IT workforce. It can fulfill your recruitment needs and offer a smooth candidate assessment experience by utilizing the best tools for efficient hiring.

# How To Test Problem Solving Skills In Tech Interview

Tech recruiters can now conduct high quality & maximum conversion driven problem solving skills assessments in for quality technical hiring.
By
|
Updated on
January 18, 2025
Table of Content
Schedule Free DemoTry WeCP for Free

Summarize with AI

Chat GPT
Perplexity
Claude
Grok
TL;DR

Problem-solving skills are among the most important skills that recruiters look for in job candidates. Problem-solving abilities demonstrate self-sufficiency and the ability to implement solutions that drive a business’s success.

We all face challenges at work daily. It could be solving an issue for a customer, designing an application, or supporting others. Organizations seek candidates who can identify strategies and ways to tackle work difficulties that may arise. This is why testing problem-solving skills pre-interview is critical in the workplace, especially in the dynamic IT industry.

## What is a problem-solving skill?

Problem-solving is a soft skill. A personal strength. It is not a learned skill through school or training. But candidates can improve their skills by familiarizing themselves with frequent challenges and learning from mentors.

The best problem solvers are proactive in anticipating future issues and take steps to avoid or minimize the consequences.

Problem-solving abilities are related to other skills that include analytical, innovative, and creative thinking, level-headedness, initiative, perseverance, teamwork, adaptability, and flexibility. These are the key competencies of a candidate’s skill set that show reasoning capabilities of evaluating positive and negative solutions to any problem.

## How to test problem-solving skills in an interview?

The purpose of a problem-solving skills assessment is for recruiters to assess if a candidate responds to scenarios logically and effectively. Recruiters also want to distinguish between results-oriented candidates and those who buckle under pressure.

The conventional approach

Traditionally, the interview stage provided an opportunity for the recruiter to understand how candidates gather data and analyze a situation where problem-solving test questions focused on past experiences and hypothetical situations. It allowed the candidate to talk about how they would approach a particular problem.

A Q&A session between recruiter and candidate gave some insight into the candidate’s problem-solving abilities. But it is not an objective nor a practical, real-life application to demonstrate these skills. Recruiters don’t fully understand how a candidate assessed the scenario and what steps they took to formulate a solution.

An effective online way

Using an online skills test recruiters can observe how potential candidates apply their problem-solving skills. For example, while hiring a Software Engineer, recruiters can assign a programming test to candidates and successfully evaluate their ability to fix a software bug.

These skill tests are suitable for any job role. They are particularly designed and tailored to see how candidates handle difficult situations they will likely face on the job.

## Connection between problem-solving and analytical thinking

Problem-solving requires the ability to think logically, as well as recall and apply facts and expertise. By breaking down the given material into manageable components and logically organize the information, the candidate’s capacity to analyze and comprehend it from various viewpoints is tested.

Numerical Ability

The ability to interpret and comprehend numbers and related symbols to perform fundamental arithmetic operations is assessed. The assessments can include interpreting graphs and tables, and numerical reasoning challenges that show the candidate’s logic and rationality.

Critical Thinking

The candidate’s capacity to identify and analyze problems by gathering and assessing relevant data to arrive at a suitable conclusion is put to the test. These assessments help recruiters better understand how candidates obtain information from different sources and evaluate data to make business-oriented decisions and communicate their findings.

## What skills do candidates need to be good at problem-solving?

Candidates with great problem-solving skills have a combination of both analytical and creative thinking. They’re comfortable with making decisions and confident enough to rise to challenges in the workplace.

These candidates possess a combination of analytical, creative, critical thinking skills and a high level of attention to detail, along with strong fundamentals. As a result, they will quickly identify problems when they arise and identify the most effective solutions. They’ll also identify the factors and forces that might have caused the problem and instigate changes to mitigate future challenges.

## What is a good example of problem-solving?

Some of the good problem-solving skills examples include a candidate’s understanding of the problem clearly before jumping into solving it, sorting out a technical problem, resolving a bug, serving a demanding client, or acting as a mentor for new interns and explaining the problem in simple terms.

## What are problem-solving skills tests?

Many organizations use problem-solving skills interview questions to select the right candidates for their job roles. However, the most effective way to assess problem-solving skills is with problem-solving tests.

Problem-solving skills tests provide an objective way to evaluate a candidate’s essential skill sets in a way that isn’t practically possible during an interview.

Tests like WeCP’s problem-solving skills testing assist organizations in finding productive candidates who can quickly filter the key elements of the problem and work through it to get a defined outcome. By presenting candidates with a broad range of questions related to different problem-solving scenarios, hiring managers and recruiters can select their candidates based on an intensive assessment of each skill level.

In a nutshell, WeCP’s problem-solving skill tests allow you to recruit candidates who are cognitively and analytically equipped to handle anything that may come their way.

## Assess problem-solving skills with WeCP

Having the right problem-solving skills is mandatory in today’s technology-driven businesses. If you like to see areas where we strongly recommend our customers to use a problem-solving test, check out this category of skills assessments. With WeCP recruiters can monitor the candidates’ progress in real-time and pull detailed reports for analysis to expedite and ease the selection process.

Get in touch with us today to learn how you can best evaluate your candidates’ abilities to apply problem-solving skills in developing and executing viable solutions. We’ll help use our carefully crafted skill maps to evaluate technical and problem-solving skills in candidates.
